stories.title: Longitudinal evidence for decreasing statistical learning abilities across childhood
stories.description: Statistical learning enables us to identify patterns in our environment and predict future events, thereby supporting a range of motor, cognitive, and linguistic skills. Despite its significance, the developmental trajectory of statistical learning has remained unclear due to a lack of comprehensive longitudinal studies. Cross-sectional research has hinted at enhanced statistical learning in children up to 11-13 years, followed by a decline into adulthood, yet definitive insights require a longitudinal approach. Our study addresses this gap by assessing statistical learning in the same participants at ages 7, 8, 11, and 14. Utilising linear mixed models and latent class analyses, we observe a decline in statistical learning with age, and find that higher executive functions—cognitive functions that underlie higher-order goal-directed behaviour—are associated with this decline. This study provides evidence that statistical learning is more effective in early childhood, offering insights into the developmental trajectory of this fundamental cognitive ability. Through statistical learning, people extract patterns from the environment to predict future events. In a longitudinal study, the authors show that statistical learning declines with age and that higher executive functions are linked to this decline.

stories.title: CLAUNet-LFB0-CBAM a deep learning framework for explainable liver fibrosis stage classification from ultrasound images
stories.description: Automated liver fibrosis staging through ultrasound images is still difficult owing to low contrast, speckle artifacts, and minor differences between successive stages. We propose a hybrid deep learning architecture named CLAUNet-LFB0-CBAM for multi-class liver fibrosis classification from ultrasound images. The method uses a preprocessing pipeline step followed by an augmented EfficientNet-B0 network with CBAM. Moreover, to deal with class imbalance issue, the method employs weighted cross-entropy loss and weighted random sampling, combined with augmentation techniques. The proposed network is compared with baseline architectures like VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, and EfficientNet-B0 within identical experimental conditions. Experimental results show that the proposed method provides superior results in terms of 99.05% accuracy, 0.980 F1-score, and 0.9987 AUC, surpassing all evaluated baseline architectures under identical experimental conditions. Importantly, the performance improvement is achieved mainly in intermediate liver fibrosis stages which are crucial for clinical evaluation. Grad-CAM analysis supports that the network learns the appropriate features from anatomical liver regions. Moreover, the network achieves lightweight implementation with only around 4.8 million parameters.

stories.title: An explainable ensemble machine learning approach for coefficient of compressibility prediction of Chengdu clay
stories.description: Accurate prediction of the coefficient of compressibility (av) for regional clays remains a fundamental challenge in geotechnical engineering. Focusing on Chengdu clays, this study proposes a machine learning framework that integrates physically constrained data augmentation, differentiated hyperparameter optimization, and interpretability analysis. Based on 338 experimental datasets, a hybrid optimization strategy (Grid Search + Bayesian Optimization) is employed to ensure fair model comparison. The statistical significance of performance differences is rigorously validated using 30 iterations of Monte Carlo cross-validation combined with paired t-tests. Generalization capability is assessed via spatial grouping cross-validation, accompanied by Bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification. Results demonstrate that LightGBM achieves the highest predictive accuracy (test R2 = 0.8817), significantly outperforming comparison models (p < 0.05). XGBoost exhibits comparable accuracy (R2 = 0.8805), while Random Forest demonstrates superior robustness in spatial cross-validation (R2 = 0.7273). Multi-model analysis consistently identifies water content and liquidity index as the dominant factors governing av, with cumulative contribution exceeding 95%. SHAP analysis confirms both factors exhibit monotonically positive effects with approximate additivity. Tree-based models yield Bootstrap confidence intervals with mean widths ranging from 0.0526 to 0.0653 MPa-1, providing essential risk references for engineering practice. This study not only delivers a reliable predictive tool for av of Chengdu clays but also establishes a reproducible, physically guided, and statistically rigorous paradigm for regional geotechnical machine learning research.

stories.title: Implications for the involvement of a CCN-like gene in the initial process of adult newt limb regeneration
stories.description: The cellular communication network (CCN) family consists of secreted proteins that regulate diverse biological processes. Newt-specific CCN (nsCCN) was long considered a unique newt factor involved in the regeneration of body parts. In this study, we demonstrate that nsCCN is not a canonical CCN member but instead belongs to a previously unrecognized sister group—CCN-like factors—that are conserved in amphibians but were lost in amniotes. To elucidate its role in adult newt limb regeneration, nsCCN-expressing cells were characterized using immunostaining and single-cell RNA-seq. We found that peripheral blood thrombocytes predominantly express nsCCN, with additional expression detected in presumed myeloid immune cells within the blastema. Regenerating limb immunohistochemistry, alongside in vitro time-lapse imaging, suggests that thrombocytes activate locally upon amputation, secreting nsCCN during blood coagulation. Furthermore, because intravenous anti-nsCCN antibody injection delayed the initiation of blastema growth, blood cell dynamics were investigated. Our results suggest that as the wound epidermis covers the amputation surface, nsCCN promotes blood influx and circulation into the interstitial space where blastema cells subsequently accumulate. Taken together, these findings reveal how nsCCN ensures proper blastema formation, potentially by facilitating thrombus fibrinolysis within local vasculature and regulating the extracellular environment through interstitial blood circulation.

Govee is also releasing a new version of its COB Strip Light Pro, which costs $169.99 and uses a chip-on-board design to smooth out the spotty look of standard LED strip lights. They have slightly denser LED placement than the previous version.

stories.description: Ok, here's the pitch - take a slightly zany Irish comedian and shove him into a classroom full of school kids aged from six to 12 years old, point a camera at them and watch the chats and the giggles flow.
